responses: Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers to the simulation of human intelligence in machines programmed to think, reason, learn, and solve problems like humans. It spans subfields like Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Robotics, and Natural Language Processing.

AI is categorized into: 1) Narrow/Weak AI (specialized in one task, like chatbots or image recognition), 2) General AI (AGI - human-level adaptability across any domain), and 3) Super AI (hypothetical intelligence surpassing humans).

AI works by combining large amounts of structured and unstructured data with intelligent, iterative processing algorithms, allowing software to learn automatically from patterns or features in the data.

responses: Machine Learning (ML) is a subset of AI that enables systems to learn and improve from experience without being explicitly programmed. Instead of hardcoded rules, ML models learn patterns from historical data.

The three primary paradigms of Machine Learning are: 1) Supervised Learning (labeled data, e.g., Classification & Regression), 2) Unsupervised Learning (unlabeled data, e.g., Clustering & Dimensionality Reduction), and 3) Reinforcement Learning (reward/penalty agent-environment interaction).
In traditional programming, you feed Data and Rules to get Answers. In Machine Learning, you feed Data and Answers to get Rules (the trained model)!

responses: Deep Learning is a specialized branch of Machine Learning based on Artificial Neural Networks with multiple hidden layers (hence 'deep'). It excels at automatically extracting representations from complex unstructured data like images, audio, and text.

Key architectures in Deep Learning include: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for vision, Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN/LSTM) for sequential data, and Transformer architectures (attention mechanism) which power modern LLMs.

Deep Learning automatically learns feature representations at progressive levels of abstraction, eliminating the need for manual feature engineering that is common in classical ML, but it requires much larger datasets and GPU acceleration.

responses: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is an interdisciplinary field of AI, computer science, and linguistics focused on enabling computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language.

A typical NLP pipeline involves: 1) Text Cleaning (lowercasing, punctuation removal), 2) Tokenization (splitting into words), 3) Stopword Filtering & Lemmatization, 4) Vectorization (e.g., TF-IDF or Embeddings), and 5) Machine Learning classification or generation.
This chatbot uses NLTK for tokenization and lemmatization, Scikit-learn's TF-IDF Vectorizer to convert sentences into numerical feature vectors, and Logistic Regression to classify user intents!

Python dominates AI and Data Science because of its rich scientific libraries (NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow), simple syntax that accelerates prototyping, and active community support.

responses: For your project viva: 1) State the problem statement and real-world relevance clearly, 2) Explain the end-to-end pipeline (Preprocessing -> TF-IDF -> Logistic Regression -> Response Selection), 3) Justify your design choices (e.g., why TF-IDF over simple bag-of-words), and 4) Present actual evaluation metrics (F1-score, accuracy, confusion matrix).
Use the STAR technique (Situation, Task, Action, Result) when answering situational or project-oriented questions. It gives structured, persuasive proof of your hands-on problem-solving abilities.

If you encounter a question you don't know: Stay calm, articulate your thought process aloud, state relevant known principles, and avoid guessing blindly. Interviewers value scientific reasoning over guesswork!

responses: Cloud Computing is the on-demand delivery of computing services—including servers, storage, databases, networking, and software—over the Internet ('the cloud') with pay-as-you-go pricing (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure).

An API (Application Programming Interface) allows different software applications to communicate with each other. RESTful APIs use standard HTTP verbs (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) to transfer state representations (often JSON).

Git is a distributed version control system that tracks changes in source code during software development, enabling branching, collaboration, history audits, and seamless merging via platforms like GitHub.

In modern web architecture, the Frontend handles visual presentation and user interaction (HTML, CSS, JS), while the Backend processes business logic, NLP/ML models, and database persistence (Flask, Python, SQL).
